items.title: [darkreading.com] CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler to combine device and network defenses
items.content_html: CrowdStrike agreed on Nov. 23 to acquire Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock transaction, combining security monitoring on devices with controls over the networks those devices, employees and AI agents use to reach applications and data. The companies say the combination would help security teams track activity across both ends of a connection as businesses deploy AI agents with access to corporate systems. CrowdStrike plans to bring Zscaler’s network telemetry into its Falcon security information and event management system and use the combined data to support its SafeMind security models. CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz described an example in which an agent accesses sensitive information on a device and sends it to an unapproved AI model: endpoint monitoring could flag the agent’s behavior while network inspection identifies its destination. The companies already have 16 technology integrations and about 2,000 shared customers, but analysts and customer advisers questioned whether a single platform would maintain service performance and compatibility with other vendors. The businesses will remain independent until shareholders and regulators approve the deal; the companies expect it to close in the second half of CrowdStrike’s fiscal 2028.
